title: Activation Hub: canonical SDK sample kits, release notes cadence, and GTM orchestration for streaming & function APIs
creator: Amira Patel
body:
Summary: Build an "Activation Hub" — a canonical onboarding surface for SDK users that bundles: (1) canonical sample kits for function-calling, structured output, and streaming patterns; (2) a coordinated release-notes cadence and snippet library for docs and SDKs; and (3) a GTM/enablement checklist for partner/onboarding teams. Goal is to reduce time-to-first-success for new SDK adopters by providing curated, production-ready examples and a single place for copy + code.

Scope:
- Canonical sample kits (TypeScript, Python, Go) covering: function-calling end-to-end, streaming incremental rendering + reconnection, structured JSON/Schema outputs, error handling & retry best practices, and migration notes from previous SDK versions.
- Release notes cadence: standardized snippets per SDK change type (breaking/minor/patch), automated changelog links, and cross-linking to console/Runtime release notes.
- GTM orchestration: pre-approved email/snippet copy for in-product notifications, partner onboarding checklist, and engineering slates for code samples to ship with releases.

Deliverables:
1) repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-activation-hub (canonical samples + README + runnable scripts).
2) Confluence playbook: "Activation Hub — GTM & Release Notes" with mapping to marketing/partner assets.
3) Snippet library in docs site with copy+code pairing for each supported language.
4) Small design kit for in-console onboarding flow (DES deliverable).

Acceptance criteria:
- All three language sample kits run via a single bootstrap script and produce identical outputs for the function-calling example.
- Release-note snippet templates for breaking/minor/patch are created and validated by PM and Docs.
- Console in-product banner and partner email copy reviewed and pre-approved by Legal & Growth.
- Measurements: 25% reduction in time-to-first-api-success in pilot cohort (internal).

Timeline & milestones:
- Week 1 (2026-02-20 to 2026-02-26): final scope sign-off, design kickoff, repo skeleton.
- Week 2 (2026-02-27 to 2026-03-05): core samples for function-calling and streaming (TS + Py).
- Week 3 (2026-03-06 to 2026-03-12): Go samples, release-notes templates, docs integration.
- Week 4 (2026-03-13 to 2026-03-19): internal pilot, iteration, legal review for messaging.
- Week 5 (2026-03-20 to 2026-03-27): staging release + launch runbook dry-run.
- Target public roll: 2026-04-01 alongside SDK 2026.04 release.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: Function-calling API surface differences between languages create drift. Mitigation: single reference spec (JSON schema) for sample outputs + CI that validates outputs across runtimes.
- Risk: Docs/SDK release cadence mismatch. Mitigation: release-note templates and a pre-release sync meeting every release sprint.

Stakeholders & reviewers:
- Eng leads: Priya Sharma (runtime) and Marcus Lee (sdk).
- Design: Lina Chen.
- Docs & DX: Omar Reyes.
- Growth & GTM: Sara Nguyen.
- Legal: Priya Rao.

Notes about trade-offs and decisions:
- Decision 2026-03-02: We will prioritize TypeScript and Python for the pilot language set due to highest usage telemetry. Go will follow in Week 3. Rationale: maximize impact for initial pilot and reduce scope. (Reviewed by Marcus and Lina, approved.)
- Trade-off: We will not implement a full interactive tutorial in the first iteration — instead we will provide a runnable CLI bootstrap. This keeps the initial scope manageable and allows us to iterate on telemetry from the CLI flows.

Open questions:
- Do we ship code samples inside the main SDK repo or keep a separate activation-hub repo? (Current leaning: separate repo for faster independent iteration; final decision after ENG feedback.)
- Should we auto-link console onboarding to the hub via a short tokenized URL? (Requires security review for tokens.)

Metrics & success criteria:
- Adoption: # of unique projects that run the bootstrap script within 30 days after rollout.
- Quality: pass rate for sample kit CI validation across languages.
- GTM: % of new trial accounts that interact with the Activation Hub during onboarding.

How this ties to other initiatives:
- Aligns to SDK-Surface-2026 and runtime-1.18 improvements (batching & streaming docs).
- Will be referenced by Dedicated onboarding and Private deployment playbooks for customers who need on-prem examples.

Delivery notes:
- Engineering will own the canonical samples and CI. Design will provide a small 2-screen onboarding flow and microcopy. Docs will embed snippet library into the SDK docs site. Growth will prepare two partner email templates and an in-product banner.

Longer-term: Consider adding an interactive sandbox and telemetry-driven sample recommendations (advanced patterns tailored to user workload).
